Treat "likely-relevant recent bug reports" as secondary evidence: they may or may not be relevant. Use them only if they help; otherwise, you may ignore them.

Some identifiers in the current bug report may be anonymized with placeholders (e.g., C#.M#). If the same token (e.g., C1) appears multiple times, it consistently refers to the same class (C) or method (M) throughout the report. These tokens are not complete qualified names. Title: Diagnosis
Details: The corresponding issue report describes that tooltip text in the UI is displayed with HTML entities such as " instead of the intended characters. This strongly suggests a missing escaping or decoding step in tooltip generation. Inspecting the implementation of StandardToolTipTagFragmentGenerator.generateToolTipFragment reveals that it directly returns the toolTipText without applying any escaping. Recent issue reports mention similar encoding or escaping problems in related UI components, reinforcing the suspicion that this method lacks proper handling. The behavior observed in the code matches the issue report's symptoms, indicating that missing escaping in this method is the likely root cause.

After providing this diagnosis, you will be prompted to suggest which methods would be the best locations to be fixed. The answers should be in the form of `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` without commentary (one per line), as your answer will be automatically processed before finally being presented to the user.

messages.content:
Title: Diagnosis
Details: The failure observed in the test `testNestedJDOM` and the issue report indicating that JXPath trims string values from XML nodes can be traced to the method `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()`. By examining this method, we see multiple occurrences where text node values are explicitly trimmed using either `getTextTrim()` or `String.trim()` calls. Specifically:

- Line 240: For `Element` nodes, `getTextTrim()` is called, which by convention trims leading and trailing whitespace from the element's text content.
- Line 245: For `Comment` nodes, the text is explicitly trimmed with `String.trim()`.
- Line 250 and 253: For `Text` and `CDATA` nodes, `getTextTrim()` is used again, which trims whitespace.
- Line 258: For `ProcessingInstruction`, the data string is trimmed.

This accounts for the behavior where values such as `<value> 12324 56</value>` lose leading and trailing whitespace because `getTextTrim()` and explicit `trim()` calls remove those spaces. The comment nodes and processing instructions are also treated similarly.

The test case expects that the original spacing is preserved, but the current implementation systematically removes leading/trailing spaces, which causes the test failure and the reported bug.

Therefore, the root cause of the bug is that `JDOMNodePointer.getValue()` is aggressively trimming string values from the underlying JDOM nodes instead of preserving the original text content as-is.

No other relevant recent bug reports are available to contradict or refine this diagnosis, so the focus should be on this method.

Based on the available information, provide the signatures of the most likely culprit methods for the bug. Your answer will be processed automatically, so make sure to only answer with the accurate signatures of all likely culprits (in `ClassName.MethodName(ArgType1, ArgType2, ...)` format), without commentary (one per line).
